chunks: From him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Regarding

A man took dirhams from another man to perform Hajj on his behalf, but spent them. When the time for Hajj arrived, that man (the employer) was unable to afford anything. The Imam said: 'He should find a way and perform Hajj on behalf of his employer, as he assumed responsibility for it.' He was asked: 'If he is unable?' He said: 'If he has a Hajj obligation (for himself) with God, he should take it from him and assign it to the one from whom he took the Hajj obligation.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if an agent spends the money given for Hajj and the employer cannot pay again?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* outlines the principle of *daman* (guarantee) in Hajj agency, where the agent remains liable for the ritual if the principal defaults. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that if the agent cannot raise funds, he may discharge the principal's obligation by performing his own obligatory Hajj (*hajj al-mufrad*) on the principal's behalf, effectively transferring his personal religious debt. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic view of Hajj as a transferable right (*haqq*) that can be settled through the agent's own fulfilled duty.
